items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: And they had this little drummer they called Rastus

ctx.x: Well, that started years ago. It was -- that was called showmanship. And in 1933, I worked with a show, and this act had been on RKO and it was one of the biggest acts in the country, called Norman Thomas' Quintet. And they had this little drummer they called Rastus, and he was about -- oh, I guess he was about four-something feet, and

weighed about 85 pounds. Real, real little bitty guy, but, oh, was he agile. And he would take the sticks and he would juggle them, do four and five -- you know they used to have the thing where they'd put them on the ground.
